key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed faying-surface geometry combined with tuned DDFW parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 joint strength, and a deep learning model can predict tensile performance from process settings with moderate accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive applications by pairing joint-geometry design with process optimization.
method: L18 orthogonal array experiments on AA2024-T351 using a customized engine lathe
Varied friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time
Trained deep learning predictors including an ensemble residual network, compact attention network, and adaptive multiscale network
evidence_signal: The best condition achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, while the ensemble residual network reached the highest prediction accuracy with R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive performance is promising but not highly deterministic, so the model should be validated on larger, more diverse welding datasets before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
